html:
A Persian theologian, lawyer and mystic from Tus who is among the most influential thinkers in Sunni Islam. He brought Sufi mysticism into the mainstream and challenged the philosophers who followed Aristotle.

In 1091 the vizier Nizam al-Mulk of the Seljuk Empire made him head teacher at the Nizamiyya college in Baghdad, the top post of its day. Four years later a crisis of doubt left him unable to speak, and he quit, spending years as a wandering Sufi in Damascus, Jerusalem and Mecca. His short autobiography, Deliverance from Error, tells this story.

In The Incoherence of the Philosophers he attacked Avicenna and other followers of Aristotle on points such as the eternity of the world, saying reason alone could not settle them. Averroes answered with The Incoherence of the Incoherence. His great work, The Revival of the Religious Sciences, joined law, theology and inner devotion. He shaped Islamic thought for centuries and was read by Jewish and Christian scholars too.
